chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abbad ibn Suhayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was negligent in paying his zakat during his lifetime, and when death approached him, he calculated all that he had neglected of the obligatory zakat, then bequeathed that it be paid out, so it should be given to whom it is due. He (the Imam) said: 'It is permissible; that is taken from all the wealth. It is like a debt; if it were upon him, the heirs have no share until what he bequeathed of the zakat is paid.' It was said to him: 'And if he bequeathed the Hajj of Islam?' He said: 'It is permissible; Hajj is performed for him from all the wealth.'
ai.seo_question: How is unpaid zakat or bequeathed Hajj handled in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the context of *iqrar* (acknowledgment) during illness, establishing that unpaid zakat is a divine debt (*dayn Allāh*) prioritized over bequests and inheritance shares. This principle ensures the fulfillment of obligatory duties before the distribution of the estate, mirroring the treatment of Hajj if bequeathed, thereby emphasizing the continuity of financial worship obligations beyond death.
